title: Homogeneous coordinate ring dimensions equal twisted Euler characteristics
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $N\ge0$, let $B=k[z_0,\ldots,z_N]$ be graded by total degree, and let $J\subseteq B$ be a homogeneous ideal. Put $A=B/J=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}A_m$ with the induced grading, and let $i:Z=\operatorname{Proj}(A)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ be the closed subscheme defined by $J$ [def-pc-proj, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $\mathcal O_Z(m)=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_k}(m)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback], where on the specified model $\mathbf P^N_k=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ the sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_k}(m)=\widetilde{B(m)}$ is the Proj twisting sheaf [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Then there is $m_0\ge0$ such that $\dim_kA_m=\chi(Z,\mathcal O_Z(m))$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic] for every $m\ge m_0$. In particular the polynomial eventually equal to $m\mapsto\dim_kA_m$ depends only on the closed subscheme $Z$, not on the homogeneous ideal $J$ defining it. The ideal $J$ need not be saturated, and $Z$ may be empty, in which case both sides vanish for $m\gg0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG7 (lemma-recover-tail-graded-module), applied to the finite graded $B$-module $A$, with varieties.tex Tag 08AE (lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0) and coherent.tex Tag 01YS (lemma-coherent-projective) (4) for the vanishing of higher cohomology of large twists.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-coordinate-quotient-section-polynomial-tail] to the actual quotient $A=B/J$. With $L_m=\mathcal O_Z(m)$ this gives $a\ge0$, a polynomial $P_J$, and for $m\ge a$ a $k$-linear isomorphism $A_m\cong H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z(m))$ with $P_J(m)=\dim_k A_m$. The chart comparison in that statement uses the pulled-back ambient Proj twist specified here, so no saturation of $J$ occurs.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, for the actual quotient graded ring; constructions.tex Tag 01MT, lemma-apply-modules, and Tag 01N1, lemma-surjective-graded-rings-generated-degree-1-map-proj, for the chartwise pullback comparison; algebra.tex Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, for the eventual polynomial.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-twist-euler-section-uniqueness] with $X=Z$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_Z$. The structure sheaf is quasi-coherent and has the finite presentation $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus0}\to\mathcal O_Z\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal O_Z\to0$; tensoring with it is the unit identification, so $E_m=\mathcal O_Z(m)$. For $m\ge b$ the cited statement gives $\chi(Z,\mathcal O_Z(m))=\dim_k H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z(m))$. Taking $m_0=\max(a,b)$ and the equality in step 1 proves the required coordinate/Euler equality and eventual polynomial existence.

Uniqueness and the empty case use the elementary rational-polynomial root argument in the returned parent proof, step 6 (agent argument).

proof.text: For two homogeneous ideals defining the same closed subscheme of this fixed projective space, identify their quotient Proj schemes with that closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$; their pulled-back twists are therefore the same $i^*\widetilde{B(m)}$. Step 1 for each ideal says that its polynomial agrees eventually with this one section-dimension function. The uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-projective-twist-euler-section-uniqueness] gives equality of the polynomials. If $Z=\varnothing$, its section and Euler functions are zero by that same node, so step 1 gives $A_m=0$ eventually and the polynomial is zero. This includes the unit ideal and unsaturated irrelevant-primary ideals.
